comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The useful probe child returned CLI semantics to the parent, including conversion failures as traceback-like stderr with exit 1; the parent then used the finding.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation gives a parallel-only pass: parallel passed 124/124 and serial passed 120/124. The concrete trajectory-level difference is invalid --b integer conversion stderr. Serial observed that the executable emits a traceback and PyInstaller-style footer for bad integer data, but its generated Node run emitted only a one-line ValueError and the agent finalized after sample and parser checks. Parallel initially lacked the footer too, then explicitly patched the traceback formatter and runtime to include a PyInstaller-style footer and verified executable and Node invalid-conversion runs side by side before final delivery. This supports a comparative contributor, not a claim that every failed serial testcase is uniquely proven from the visible logs.
parallel_contributors: The parent used the probe child and its own checks to cover more CLI edge cases than the serial final verification.
The parent patched invalid --b conversion stderr after seeing the executable's traceback and PyInstaller-style footer and then rechecked the Node output.
serial_contributors: Serial observed executable invalid-conversion behavior but implemented the Node formatter as a bare ValueError line.
Serial finalized after sample and parser checks without a passing invalid-conversion stderr parity check.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's missing traceback and PyInstaller-style footer for post-parse integer conversion is an ordinary implementation omission, not a serial coordination issue.
Parallel's extra edge-case implementation work made its delivered artifact more evaluator-aligned.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

The parent integrated all files and later patches into one /output tree; there were no separately implemented components lacking an integrator.
The required entry file and module tree were assembled by the parent and validated as the submitted artifact.
The parent owned the end-to-end path from probing through implementation, verification, and final delivery, even while using child probes.
Executable probing informed the implementation but did not block productive work into an adverse delay or unfinished deliverable; the final artifact passed.
Investigation and implementation were partly interleaved, and the investigation produced useful findings rather than leaving later work deadline-constrained or incomplete.
The critical implementation path stayed with the parent, received enough capacity, and produced a passing artifact; auxiliary review did not starve required work.
Only two children were spawned and the run did not time out; waits on the late reviewer did not exhaust the finite budget before required delivery.
No indispensable implementation scope was assigned to an overbroad child; the probe child completed and the late review child was optional review after the main behavior was fixed.
The available child outputs show the probe pursued the intended CLI behavior and returned usable findings; no known requirement omission in a child brief produced unusable work or rework.
Children were not separately producing interoperating implementation components, so there was no missing cross-agent file, export, input, output, or compatibility contract.
The useful probe result reached the parent and was used; no known finding is shown disappearing through summary or transfer and causing repeated or wrong work.
No returned handoff was too large or unstructured for the parent to consume; the substantive probe result was concise enough to guide later checks.
No parent action relied on a child report describing superseded files, requirements, or decisions; later patches were based on current checks.
There were no incompatible completed reports or contracts from multiple children that remained unadjudicated at an integration decision.
The parent did not accept completion solely on child output or file existence; it performed integrated Node/executable checks including the decisive invalid --b behavior before finalization.

A complete candidate was not stranded or left unpromoted; parent wrote the entrypoint/module tree and finalized a passing artifact.
The final traceback/footer change was followed by another invalid --b executable-vs-Node check, so no relevant merge landed after verification without a closing check.
No child completed an implementation that the parent failed to retrieve or adopt; the parent authored the implementation itself.
The late review child did not return a completed concrete verifier result; its interrupted in-progress note did not displace the parent's existing integrated checks or create an unmet requirement.
No required child failed with unfinished indispensable scope; after interrupting optional review, the parent already owned and completed verification and delivery.
The completed probe child result was received and used; the late review child was not a completed result available to ignore.
The parent waited on the late review child, listed and messaged it, then interrupted it; routine waiting after a verified candidate did not hide available progress that would change required work.
Children did not write competing implementation paths; the parent controlled the source tree and no overlapping design reconciliation was required.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file with one needing to reconcile the other's concurrent change.
No agent replaced non-entry source owned or produced by another agent; observed patches are parent-owned revisions.
The entrypoint and submitted artifact were created and modified by the parent, not overwritten while another agent owned or used them.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
Although all actors could see /output, only the parent wrote the deliverable, and no unstable state or provenance problem from shared writes materialized.
No generated fixture, cache, temporary path, or child artifact was consumed as a stable reference in a way that contaminated implementation or verification.
